title: LLM-QRP: Quantization for Reasoning Preservation in Small LLMs
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated exceptional capabilities in textual inference, but their deployment on edge devices is limited by high computation and memory overhead. To address this, we propose LLM-QRP (Quantization for Reasoning Preservation), a layer-aware mixed-precision quantization framework designed to reduce model size while preserving reasoning performance. Unlike uniform post-training quantization methods, LLM-QRP identifies and preserves critical “thinking” layers by analyzing layer-wise logit evolution and entropy dynamics across transformer blocks. These signals are combined into a unified reasoning importance score that ranks layers according to their contribution during inference. We then apply an empirical mixed-precision strategy that assigns higher precision to high-scoring layers and lower precision to less important layers, targeting the Pareto frontier between model compression and reasoning performance. Experiments on multiple small models using GSM8K and TruthfulQA show that LLM-QRP reduces VRAM usage while maintaining near-baseline reasoning performance and outperforming standard uniform 4-bit quantization. The resulting models aim to provide the most compressed model at a given reasoning-performance level, enabling efficient deployment on resource-constrained hardware without significant degradation in reasoning ability.
